uncited: This method computes exact gradient vectors for local shading (BRDF) in volume rendering by evaluating analytic derivatives of the underlying box-spline basis function, avoiding the inaccuracies and extra memory bandwidth of finite differences.

It sets itself apart from [Analytic Gradient Computation](2167-analytic-gradient-computation.md) by specifically exploiting the symmetry and structure of Face-Centered Cubic (FCC) box-spluses to reuse the 19 samples already fetched for scalar evaluation, whereas finite difference methods require six additional full spline evaluations.
- Volume data $V$ defined on an FCC grid.
- Evaluation point $x$ in continuous space.
- The set of direction vectors $\Xi_{\text{fcc}}$ defining the FCC box-spline $M_{\text{fcc}}$.
- Gradient vector $\nabla(V * M_{\text{fcc}})(x)$.
- The scalar value is computed as $s(x) = V * M_{\text{fcc}}(x)$.
- The gradient is computed using three directional derivatives $d_{110}, d_{101}, d_{011}$ along vectors $\xi_{110}, \xi_{101}, \xi_{011}$.
- Derivative kernels $M_\xi$ are defined as sums of two box-splines.
Due to symmetry, only the B-spline (BB) coefficients for $M_{110}$ are explicitly stored/computed; others are derived via permutation.
- $M_{110}$ requires handling three polynomial piece types: $\tau_0, \tau_2, \tau_4$.
**Fetch Samples:** Retrieve the 19 voxel values $V$ required for the evaluation of the FCC box-spline $M_{\text{fcc}}$ at point $x$.
These samples cover the support of $M_{\text{fcc}}$.
**Compute Directional Derivatives:** Calculate the three directional derivatives $d_\xi = V * M_\xi$ for $\xi \in \{\xi_{110}, \xi_{101}, \xi_{011}\}$.
- Evaluate $M_\xi$ using the de Casteljau algorithm.
- For $M_{110}$, determine the polynomial piece type ($\tau_0, \tau_2, \text{or } \tau_4$) based on the local grid position.
The method is deterministic based on the grid and data.
The analytic method avoids this entirely.
- **Polynomial Piece Identification:** Correctly identifying the polynomial piece type ($\tau_0, \tau_2, \tau_4$) is critical for using the correct BB-coefficients.
- **Support Mismatch:** While the support of $M_\xi$ is a subset of $M_{\text{fcc}}$, care must be taken to align the coefficients with the correct fetched samples.
This variant uses the analytic gradient to compute normal vectors for isosurface rendering.
- Time complexity is dominated by the evaluation of the quadratic derivative kernels using the de Casteljau algorithm.
- Memory complexity is identical to scalar evaluation as it reuses the same 19 samples.
The method is specific to FCC box-spluses.
- Use when high-quality normals are required for shading or isosurface rendering and performance is a concern.
- Do not use if the volume data is not represented by FCC box-spluses.
It addresses the limitations of finite difference gradient estimation in the context of FCC grid volume rendering, leveraging the mathematical properties of box-spluses to provide exact derivatives.
